search_log: Searched site:simonandschuster.com and "Cloud Cuckoo Land" Anthony Doerr excerpt/first chapter; the publisher page confirmed the work and strands, while CBS and Everand supplied sustained prose.
Searched "Cloud Cuckoo Land" third person, narrator, and point of view; opened BookBrowse, BookRags, Berkeley Fiction Review, and an ebook preview rather than relying on snippets.

Searched "Cloud Cuckoo Land" epistolary, diary, frame narrative, multiple narrators, and alternating point of view; results described braided character viewpoints and an embedded fictional manuscript, not sustained first- or second-person base sections.

Searched for first-person folios and story-within-a-story structure; sources confirmed that Aethon's folios are interspersed embedded material, so their local first-person passages do not make the book alternating.

Targeted exact-quote searches for ambiguous first-person and we passages produced no stronger contextual source; they were treated conservatively as dialogue, embedded material, or unclear rather than as base narration.
person_note: The controlling narration rotates among five focal characters but remains third person: the quotes repeatedly narrate Zeno, Anna, Omeir, Konstance, and Seymour externally while entering their perceptions. The authorized opening material independently shows the same construction across several named strands, and multiple whole-book sources explicitly describe a rotating third-person narrative. Apparent first- or second-person counterexamples are character speech, generic aphorisms, free-direct thought framed by he thinks, or the embedded Aethon manuscript. The only remaining uncertainty concerns the exact local boundaries of two clipped we-passages, neither of which supplies credible evidence of a sustained non-third-person base section.
